A compound of Xe and F is found to have $53.5\%$ of Xe. What is oxidation number of Xe in this compound ?
solution:
Xe $= 53.5\%$ $\therefore$ F $= 46.5\%$

Relative number of atoms: Xe $= \dfrac{53.5}{131.2} = 0.4$ and F $= \dfrac{46.5}{19} = 2.4$

Simple ratio Xe $= 1$ and F $= 6$; molecular formula is $\text{XeF}_6$. O.N. of Xe is $+6$.

In nucleophilic substitution reaction, order of halogens as incoming (attacking) nucleophile is: $\text{I}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{Cl}^-$. The order of halogens as departing nucleophile should be :
solution:
Since the leaving group breaks away as a base, it is easier to displace weaker bases than stronger bases. The basic strength of the given groups is in the order $\text{I}^- < \text{Br}^- < \text{Cl}^-$.

Thus the order of halogen leaving groups is $\text{I}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{Cl}^-$.

$\text{Zn}^{2+}(aq) + 2e \rightleftharpoons \text{Zn}(s);\ -0.762$
$\text{Cr}^{3+}(aq) + 3e \rightleftharpoons \text{Cr}(s);\ -0.740$
$2\text{H}^+(aq) + 2e \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2(g);\ 0.00$
$\text{Fe}^{3+}(aq) + e \rightleftharpoons \text{Fe}^{2+}(aq);\ 0.770$

solution: More negative the reduction potential, higher will be the reducing property, i.e. the power to give up electrons.
